archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (injury-tested)
archetype.definition: A team whose play-by-play efficiency is in the league's top third while its record sits near the bottom, because close games, turnovers and the worst special teams in football have gone against it, and that now has to prove the efficiency survives a wave of injuries.

report.headline: A top-ten team by efficiency, losing on kicks, turnovers and now attrition.
report.take:
Strip away the 2-4 and these Rams still look like a McVay team that knows what it is doing. They rank 9th in net EPA, 3rd in yards gained per game and 3rd in yards allowed. Their offensive success rate is 6th, and the line has allowed the lowest pressure rate in the league. That is not last year's juggernaut, which led the league in net EPA and scoring, but it is a good football team. The point differential sits at -3 over six games and implies four wins, not two. A winsOverExpected of -1.97 ranks 31st, so nearly the whole gap between how they play and what they have to show for it is close-game noise.

The drivers of that gap are specific. Special teams cost them 4.89 EPA a game, dead last, and now the kicker is gone for the year with a torn ACL. They have nine turnovers, with two giveaways in four of the six games. They are 1-for-4 in one-score games: four-point losses to Denver, a three-point shootout loss to Buffalo, and an 18-16 loss to Arizona as 12.5-point favorites. That is the profile of a team bleeding points in the hidden phases rather than getting outplayed snap to snap. The one real beating was Week 1 against an unbeaten San Francisco.

What the record hides cuts both ways, though. The defense's fine yardage numbers rest on a unit that already struggled to get home: 8 sacks (27th) and a QB hit rate 30th in the league. That was with Kobie Turner and Poona Ford on the field and Myles Garrett available for only one game. Turner is headed to IR, Ford is done for the season, and Garrett's practice window isn't opening this week. Trent McDuffie, a 100% snap corner, missed Arizona. On offense, Davante Adams ruptured a hamstring and is targeting a return after the Week 11 bye. That loads more onto Puka Nacua, who already has 52 targets in four games, Kyren Williams and Tyler Higbee. The Arizona loss was the game where all of this landed at once.

Where it goes depends on whether the efficiency was the team or the roster. The protection and run blocking should hold up, and Stafford has thrown for 1,794 yards behind it. The defense is the question: a unit that wins by taking away explosives and getting off the field on third down can lose that edge fast when its front is gutted. The next four games, against the Raiders, Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals, are the window to bank wins before Green Bay, Kansas City, San Francisco and two Seattle games arrive.

strengths.title: Protection that keeps Stafford clean
strengths.body: The Rams have allowed the lowest pressure rate in the league and one of the lowest sack rates. Their stuff rate on runs ranks 3rd, so the line is winning in both phases. This is structural, and it is the most bankable thing about the team. It also means Stafford's arm, not his escapability, gets to decide games.

strengths.title: An offense that moves the chains
strengths.body: A 6th-ranked success rate and 3rd-ranked yardage show an offense that stays on schedule and controls the clock. Points per game (21st) lag the yardage badly, which points to turnovers and finishing problems rather than an inability to move. Adams' absence thins the passing tree, but the down-to-down engine is the line and the scheme.

strengths.title: A defense that takes away the top
strengths.body: No defense has been better against deep passes. The Rams rank 3rd in yards allowed, 7th in third-down rate and 7th in red-zone touchdown rate allowed. It is a bend-nothing, deny-explosives unit. How much of that survives without Turner, Ford and McDuffie is the open question for the next month.

concerns.title: Worst special teams in football
concerns.body: Losing 4.89 EPA a game on special teams is the single biggest reason a top-ten efficiency team is 2-4. In a season of close losses, that is the margin. Losing kicker Blake Grupe for the year means a newcomer inherits the job. That could help or hurt, but it adds variance in exactly the games they keep losing.

concerns.title: A defensive front in pieces
concerns.body: Even before the injuries, the pass rush was among the league's weakest at getting hits on the quarterback. Now Turner is expected on IR, Ford is out for the season and Garrett has no return in sight this week. The secondary's deep coverage has been carrying the defense. Less pressure gives quarterbacks more time to find the WR3s and checkdowns this unit already struggles with.

concerns.title: Turnovers erasing good drives
concerns.body: Nine giveaways against six takeaways leaves a -3 margin that has shown up in nearly every game. With an offense this efficient, the turnovers are the leak that turns yardage into field goals or nothing. Some of it is noise and should cool. A thinner receiver room, though, could force Stafford into tighter windows.

trend.note: The passing game has swung from big positive outings against the Giants and Bills to clearly negative ones against San Francisco and Arizona. The results have been just as uneven, with a blowout win, a blowout loss and three close losses. The Arizona loss also brought the injury wave, so the next few weeks are effectively a new sample.

nextGame.headline: Rams favored in Vegas, but their depleted front faces Cousins.
nextGame.body:
This is a clean contrast in profiles. Las Vegas can't run at all: it ranks last in run success and yards before contact, and 29th in rush EPA. Its offense lives on Kirk Cousins' passing, 5th in pass EPA. Its defense is the mirror image of the Rams' offense. It ranks 3rd in pressure rate and 3rd in takeaways, but 25th in pass EPA allowed and dead last against short passes. The Book has the Rams -4.5 with a 47.5 total indoors, though the Raiders have covered at the league's best rate.

Availability tilts toward Las Vegas more than the line suggests. The Rams go without Adams and Turner, with Ford done for the year and Garrett not yet practicing. McDuffie's return date is listed for game day, but that is an estimate after he sat out Arizona. A new kicker steps in for Grupe. The Raiders are missing DT Tonka Hemingway, a part-time interior player, and two pass catchers who hadn't played this season.
